newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two Shi'ites killed in Pakistan sectarian attacks.
newsitem.headline: Two Shi'ites killed in Pakistan sectarian attacks.

text.p: Gunmen killed two Shi'ite Moslem activists in Pakistan's central province of Punjab on Thursday in apparent sectarian violence that the provincial chief executive vowed to end by force.
Two gunmen riding a motorcycle shot Baqir Hussain Shah, a speaker on religion and a local leader of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria party, in the central Punjab city of Faisalabad, police said.
They said another Shi'ite activist, Pir Hussain Shah, was shot at his home in a village outside nearby Samundri town by two attackers who were also riding a motorcycle.

There was no immediate information about the identity of the attackers, who struck a day after unidentified gunmen hit a prayer meeting at a Sunni sect mosque in the Punjab capital Lahore, killing one man and injuring three others.
One of the three wounded men died in hospital on Thursday while another injured was in a critical condition, hospital sources said.
The shootings seemed to be the latest in a wave of attacks in Punjab blamed on rival militant factions of the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam.
Punjab Chief Minister Shahbaz Sharif said on Thursday that his provincial government had decided to raise an elite force to fight what he called "sectarian terrorism".
He told reporters after a meeting of his cabinet that the force would be selected from the existing police and would be given rigorous training in shooting and martial arts.
Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab, where militant Sunni and Shi'ite factions are engaged in a feud that officials say has cost 96 lives so far this year.
Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan that cost at least 170 lives last year.
Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of more than 135 million but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
